draft.title: Shortages and surpluses
card: When the price is below equilibrium, buyers want more than sellers offer. Some buyers miss out.
When the price is above equilibrium, sellers offer more than buyers want. Unsold stock builds up.
In a shortage, buyers compete for the limited stock, so the price tends to rise. In a surplus, sellers cut prices to clear stock, so the price tends to fall.
Either way, the price moves towards equilibrium, where the shortage or surplus is gone.

4.alt: Demand D and supply S cross at the equilibrium price P*. At a price P1 below P*, the quantity demanded is greater than the quantity supplied, which is a shortage. At a price P2 above P*, the quantity supplied is greater than the quantity demanded, which is a surplus.

draft.remember: Below equilibrium means a shortage and a rising price. Above it means a surplus and a falling price.

a.q: A bakery in Geelong prices its pies above the equilibrium price. What is likely to happen?
opts: Unsold pies build up and the price tends to fall
Buyers want more pies than offered and the price rises
Unsold pies build up and the price tends to rise
Buyers want more pies than offered and the price falls
a.why: Above equilibrium, sellers offer more than buyers want, so stock is left over and the price tends to fall. The option with a shortage is wrong because a shortage happens when the price is below equilibrium.
a.clue: Think about whether pies sell out or get left over.

b.q: Tickets to a concert in Ballarat sell out in minutes at $40, and many fans are left without one. What does this suggest, and what is likely to follow?
opts: The price is below equilibrium, so the price may rise
The price is below equilibrium, so the price may fall
The price is above equilibrium, so the price may fall
The price is above equilibrium, so the price may rise
b.why: Fans wanting more tickets than are offered is a shortage, which happens when the price is below equilibrium. Buyers compete for the tickets, so the price tends to rise. Selling out quickly does not mean the price is too high.
b.clue: Did buyers want more or less than was offered?
